subject: Extracting intensity values for a  given m/z based on diagnosis factor

messages.author: d9399aa1f4bbe32d
messages.subject: Extracting intensity values for a  given m/z based on diagnosis factor
parts:
Hi Kylie,
thanks for this great R package!  I have a question concerning extracting intensity values throughout specific pixels for a given mz-value.
I did a supervised analysis of my data. Now, I would like to extract the intensity data of some of my mz-values of interest based on the diagnosis factor(cancer,  healthy).
This is in order to later on plot them for example  in a boxplot comparing mz= 944.5 healthy vs cancer .
It would be great if you could help me on how to access the intensity values.

thanks,

best wishes
Uwe

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Extracting intensity values for a  given m/z based on diagnosis factor
parts:
Hi Uwe,

You can access the intensities as a matrix via the spectra(x) method. The rows are the m/z features and the columns are pixels. (So each column is a mass spectrum.)

Here is a simple way to achieve what you want:

library(CardinalWorkflows)
data(rcc)
intensity <- spectra(rcc.small)[features(rcc.small, mz=215),]
data <- data.frame(intensity=intensity, diagnosis=rcc.small$diagnosis)
boxplot(intensity ~ diagnosis, data=data)

First, I use the features() method to find the row ID for m/z 215, and then subset that row from the spectra() matrix.

This dataset already has the regions as a pixelData column in 'rcc.small', so I just make a new data.frame using the intensities and that column identifying regions.

Then I use the data.frame to generate a box plot.

(You could subset the spectra matrix based on the columns as well if you want to get separate vectors of intensities vectors for each region, but here it is easier to just get all of them and let the plotting function do that.)

-Kylie
